title: Does Dark Mode Actually Save Battery?
sources: Purdue University news release, 28 July 2021, 'Dark mode may not save your phone's battery life as much as you think' (Dash & Hu, MobiSys 2021): OLED screens have no backlight like LCD screens, so they draw less power showing dark pixels; switching light to dark mode at 100% brightness saves an average of 39%-47% battery power, but at 30%-50% brightness only 3%-9%; brightness largely determines the savings

LCD vs OLED basics (Purdue release; display references): an LCD lights every pixel with one backlight, so black pixels still have the backlight on; each OLED pixel emits its own light and a true-black pixel is switched off
Google, Android Dev Summit 2018 (reported by Android Authority / 9to5Google): dark themes cut OLED display power, more so at high brightness

lines.text: Does dark mode actually save your phone's battery?
Well, it depends on your screen.
Many older phones use an LCD,
where one big backlight shines behind every pixel,
so even black is still lit up.
But most newer phones use OLED,
where every pixel makes its own light,
and a black pixel just switches off.
so dark mode really can help.
One study found that at full brightness,
dark mode saves around forty percent,
it's only about three to nine percent.
So turn the brightness down first, then go dark.
